title: Constitution Breakdown #7: California AG Rob Bonta

sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Breakdown of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这是《99%隐形》对宪法的深度解析。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elizabeth Jo.
sentences.zh: 我是伊丽莎白·乔。

sentences.en: Today, we are discussing Article 4, which talks about the relationship between the states and between the states and the federal government.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论第四条，它探讨的是各州之间，以及各州与联邦政府之间的关系。

sentences.en: We're also skipping ahead a bit and adding the 10th Amendment to this conversation because that also talks about the states.
sentences.zh: 我们还会稍微跳跃一下，把第十修正案也加进这次对话，因为它也涉及各州的问题。

sentences.en: Our guest for this episode is California Attorney General Rob Bonta.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的嘉宾是加利福尼亚州总检察长罗伯·邦塔。

sentences.en: State attorneys general provide legal counsel to their state's government, oversee state prosecutions, and represent the public interest in a variety of cases.
sentences.zh: 州总检察长负责为本州政府提供法律咨询，监督州内起诉工作，并在各类案件中代表公共利益。

sentences.en: They also have the responsibility of protecting their state's citizens from federal overreach.
sentences.zh: 他们还有责任保护本州公民免受联邦政府的越权干预。

sentences.en: What constitutes an overreach can vary widely depending on the state's political leaning and who's in control of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 何为“越权”的界定，会根据各州的政治倾向以及谁在掌控联邦政府而有很大差异。

sentences.en: During the Obama and Biden administrations, red states sued the federal government over issues like Medicaid expansion and environmental regulations.
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马和拜登政府执政期间，共和党执政的州曾就医疗补助扩张和环境法规等问题起诉过联邦政府。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 而现在，

sentences.en: blue states like California have sued the Trump administration dozens of times for things like withholding federal funding and deploying the National Guard without consent of the state.
sentences.zh: 像加利福尼亚州这样的民主党执政州，已经数十次起诉特朗普政府，理由包括扣留联邦资金以及未经州政府同意部署国民警卫队等。

sentences.en: Attorney General Bonta talks about some of these lawsuits and why he believes the Constitution is on his side.
sentences.zh: 总检察长邦塔将谈论其中一些诉讼，以及他为何认为宪法站在他这一边。

sentences.en: But first, Elizabeth takes us through what we need to know about Article 4 and the 10th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但首先，伊丽莎白将带我们了解关于第四条和第十修正案我们需要知道的内容。

sentences.en: Okay, so unlike Articles 1, 2, and 3, which we've already talked about, they set up the federal government and get a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 好的，与我们之前讨论过的第一、二、三条不同，那几条确立了联邦政府的架构，因此备受关注。

sentences.en: Article 4 does not get too much love.
sentences.zh: 第四条并没有得到太多重视。

sentences.en: Most people have no idea what it's about.
sentences.zh: 大多数人根本不知道它是关于什么的。

sentences.en: It's not thought of too often, but it is an important source of powers and protections for the states.
sentences.zh: 人们很少想到它，但它却是各州权力和保护的重要来源。

sentences.en: So when we talk about the relationship between the federal government and that of the states, we refer to that structure as federalism.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论联邦政府与各州政府之间的关系时，我们称这种结构为“联邦制”。

sentences.en: And we've talked about federalism lots of times.
sentences.zh: 我们已经多次讨论过联邦制了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But maybe we could really call that vertical federalism.
sentences.zh: 但也许我们可以称之为“纵向联邦制”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there's a—well, that's because it's the federal government, sort of how it relates to each one of the 50 states.
sentences.zh: 之所以这么说，是因为这是联邦政府与50个州中每一个州的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the states have relationships with one another.
sentences.zh: 但各州之间也存在关系。

sentences.en: And Sections 1 and 2 of Article 4 are actually about the relationships among the states.
sentences.zh: 第四条的第一款和第二款实际上就是关于各州之间的关系。

sentences.en: And we can talk about that as horizontal federalism.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将其称为“横向联邦制”。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So why don't we start with Section 1?
sentences.zh: 那我们从第一款开始怎么样？

sentences.en: Roman, why don't you read Section 1?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你来读一下第一款好吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Full faith and credit shall be given in each state to the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of every other state.
sentences.zh: 各州应对其他每一州的公共法案、记录和司法程序给予充分的信任和尊重。

sentences.en: And Congress may, by general laws, prescribe the manner in which such acts, records, and proceedings shall be proved and the effect thereof.
sentences.zh: 国会可以通过一般法律，规定证明此类法案、记录和程序的方式及其效力。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's a mouthful.
sentences.zh: 这听起来挺拗口的。

sentences.en: So Section 1 is also known as the full faith and credit clause.
sentences.zh: 所以第一款也被称为“充分信任与尊重条款”。

sentences.en: And the full faith and credit clause embodies the idea that we need some kind of interstate cooperation in our system for the system to work.
sentences.zh: “充分信任与尊重条款”体现了这样一种理念：为了让我们的系统有效运作，我们需要某种州际合作。

sentences.en: And the basic idea with the full faith and credit clause is that the states are supposed to respect the laws, records, and court decisions of other states.
sentences.zh: 该条款的基本理念是，各州应当尊重其他州的法律、记录和法院判决。

sentences.en: That's the general idea.
sentences.zh: 这就是大体意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, what it means in the specifics, however, is that if, for instance, you have a state court issue a judgment in your favor,
sentences.zh: 然而，具体来说，这意味着如果，举个例子，你在一个州获得了法院的胜诉判决，

sentences.en: let's say you win a case and the court awards you damages or money, you can ask a court in another state to enforce or respect that judgment.
sentences.zh: 假设你赢了一场官司，法院判给你损害赔偿金或钱款，你可以要求另一个州的法院执行或尊重该判决。

sentences.en: Let's say if the person who owes you money now has left the state and taken their assets with them.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果欠你钱的人现在离开了该州，并带走了他们的资产。

sentences.en: The defendant doesn't get another chance to redo the case just because the dispute has essentially traveled to another state.
sentences.zh: 被告不能仅仅因为争议转移到了另一个州，就获得重新审理案件的机会。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: That's really what the clause is about.
sentences.zh: 这才是该条款的真正含义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Most of the time, though, the full faith and credit clause is mostly overlooked.
sentences.zh: 不过，大多数时候，“充分信任与尊重条款”往往被忽视。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel like a hot topic, right?
sentences.zh: 它听起来不像是个热门话题，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's sort of metabolized into our way of being.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它已经融入了我们的生活方式。

sentences.en: Like, I don't think that I'd have different rights in different states necessarily all that much.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不觉得我在不同州会有什么本质上的权利差异。

sentences.en: I just think of the United States as one big thing, which is kind of how this works in practice.
sentences.zh: 我只是把美国看作一个整体，这在实践中确实就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: That's the way it's supposed to work in theory.
sentences.zh: 理论上它本该如此运作。

sentences.en: But there are a few areas where there have been some important questions.
sentences.zh: 但在某些领域，确实存在一些重要的问题。

sentences.en: And actually, one of them is marriage.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中之一就是婚姻。

sentences.en: So in 2015, the Supreme Court decided the case of Obergefell versus Hodges.
sentences.zh: 2015年，最高法院裁决了“奥贝格费尔诉霍奇斯案”。

sentences.en: And that's the case in which the Supreme Court recognized a constitutionally protected right to same-sex marriage, right?
sentences.zh: 那是最高法院承认宪法保护同性婚姻权利的案件，对吧？

sentences.en: And so there had been a longstanding constitutionally protected right to marriage before the Obergefell case.
sentences.zh: 在奥贝格费尔案之前，宪法长期以来一直保护婚姻权利。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until 2015 that the Supreme Court formally recognized that this right also included the LGBTQ community.
sentences.zh: 但直到2015年，最高法院才正式承认这一权利也包括LGBTQ群体。

sentences.en: So that raises the question, well, what was life like before Obergefell?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：在奥贝格费尔案之前，生活是什么样的？

sentences.en: It's hard to remember.
sentences.zh: 很难回想起来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's hard to remember.
sentences.zh: 是的，很难回想起来了。

sentences.en: But the answer is that whether or not any state recognized same-sex marriages, whether the marriage occurred within the state or without the state,
sentences.zh: 但答案是，无论某个州是否承认同性婚姻，无论婚姻是在州内还是州外缔结的，

sentences.en: was often up to question and left up to individual states.
sentences.zh: 往往都是个疑问，并由各州自行决定。

sentences.en: So some states, if you recall these before times, some states recognized same-sex marriage, but other states didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你还记得那些“过去的日子”，有些州承认同性婚姻，但有些州不承认。

sentences.en: And in fact, they went further and either passed laws or changed even their state constitutions to say that marriage was only between a man and a woman within that state.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们甚至更进一步，通过法律或修改州宪法，规定在该州内婚姻只能是一男一女之间缔结的。

sentences.en: But, of course, at the same time, there was a growing movement for marriage equality to recognize that same-sex couples had rights to marriage.
sentences.zh: 但当然，与此同时，一场争取婚姻平权的运动正在兴起，旨在承认同性伴侣拥有婚姻权。

sentences.en: So what if you were part of a same-sex couple, lawfully married in one state, but then moved to a state where same-sex marriage was not legal, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你是一对同性伴侣，在一个州合法结婚，然后搬到了一个同性婚姻不合法的州，会怎样呢？

sentences.en: So prior to 2015, the answer wasn't really clear at all because, on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 在2015年之前，答案并不明确，因为一方面，

sentences.en: it's actually not clear that it's answered by the full faith and credit clause for complicated reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于复杂的原因，并不清楚“充分信任与尊重条款”是否能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But let me just put it this way.
sentences.zh: 但我换个说法。

sentences.en: On the one hand, a marriage isn't really a judgment.
sentences.zh: 一方面，婚姻并不是真正的“判决”。

sentences.en: That's the language of the clause itself.
sentences.zh: 那是条款本身的措辞。

sentences.en: A marriage is really a civil contract between two people, right?
sentences.zh: 婚姻实际上是两个人之间的民事契约，对吧？

sentences.en: The court doesn't judge that you're married.
sentences.zh: 法院并不会裁定你“已婚”。

sentences.en: No court does that.
sentences.zh: 没有法院会这样做。

sentences.en: And then second, courts allowed what's called a public policy exception to the full faith and credit clause.
sentences.zh: 其次，法院允许对“充分信任与尊重条款”进行所谓的“公共政策例外”。

sentences.en: So even if we agreed that a marriage was a judgment, which is a question, it really could be the case that a state court would say, well,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们同意婚姻是一种判决（这本身就是一个问题），州法院确实可能会说，嗯，

sentences.en: it's against the public policy of our state to recognize same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 承认同性婚姻违反了我们州的公共政策。

sentences.en: And then the court might decline to do so.
sentences.zh: 然后法院可能会拒绝承认。

sentences.en: And in 1996, Congress went even further and passed what was called the Defense of Marriage Act or DOMA, right?
sentences.zh: 1996年，国会更进一步，通过了所谓的《捍卫婚姻法案》或称DOMA，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know if you remember that.
sentences.zh: 不知道你还记不记得。

sentences.en: I do remember that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我记得，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then one of the significant things that DOMA did was to allow states to refuse to recognize same-sex marriages,
sentences.zh: DOMA所做的重要事情之一，就是允许各州拒绝承认同性婚姻，

sentences.en: even if these marriages were finalized in states where that marriage was actually illegal.
sentences.zh: 即使这些婚姻是在同性婚姻合法的州完成的。

sentences.en: Okay, so how could Congress do that?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么国会是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: Well, because of the full faith and credit clause.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为“充分信任与尊重条款”。

sentences.en: Because the clause itself doesn't just say states have to respect each other's judgments.
sentences.zh: 因为该条款本身不仅仅是说各州必须尊重彼此的判决。

sentences.en: It happens to give Congress a source of lawmaking power.
sentences.zh: 它恰好赋予了国会立法权。

sentences.en: It's called the effects clause, right?
sentences.zh: 这被称为“效力条款”，对吧？

sentences.en: So the full faith and credit clause allows Congress to prescribe the manner in which such acts, recordings, and proceedings shall be proved and the effect thereof.
sentences.zh: 所以“充分信任与尊重条款”允许国会规定证明此类法案、记录和程序的方式及其效力。

sentences.en: So it's actually not just saying, hey, states, you have to respect other states' judgments.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上不仅仅是在说：嘿，各州，你们必须尊重其他州的判决。

sentences.en: It's actually a source of federal legislative authority.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是联邦立法权的一个来源。

sentences.en: So with DOMA, it becomes legal for states to refuse to recognize otherwise legal same-sex marriages.
sentences.zh: 因此，有了DOMA，各州拒绝承认在其他地方合法的同性婚姻就变得合法了。

sentences.en: And while many states legalized discrimination against same-sex marriages, other states also began to recognize rights.
sentences.zh: 虽然许多州将针对同性婚姻的歧视合法化，但其他州也开始承认相关权利。

sentences.en: So Massachusetts became the first state to legalize same-sex marriage in 2004, and that's 11 years before the Obergefell decision in the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州在2004年成为第一个将同性婚姻合法化的州，那是在最高法院做出奥贝格费尔裁决的11年前。

sentences.en: And many states followed, but many states did not.
sentences.zh: 许多州效仿了，但也有许多州没有。

sentences.en: And then the Supreme Court did decide the case in 2015.
sentences.zh: 然后最高法院在2015年做出了裁决。

sentences.en: There, the Supreme Court said that same-sex couples have a fundamental right to marry in all states.
sentences.zh: 最高法院裁定，同性伴侣在所有州都拥有基本的结婚权。

sentences.en: So what is the effect of Obergefell, and why should we care about this anymore now that that's sort of settled?
sentences.zh: 那么奥贝格费尔案的效力是什么？既然事情已经定论，我们为什么还要关心这个？

sentences.en: Okay, well, on the one hand, the Supreme Court case does basically invalidate every state law that refused to recognize same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 好的，一方面，最高法院的裁决基本上废除了所有拒绝承认同性婚姻的州法律。

sentences.en: After the Obergefell decision, every state has to recognize the right to same-sex marriage because of the Supreme Court's decision.
sentences.zh: 奥贝格费尔裁决后，由于最高法院的决定，每个州都必须承认同性婚姻的权利。

sentences.en: It's constitutionalized this particular right to marry.
sentences.zh: 它将这种特定的结婚权宪法化了。

sentences.en: And Obergefell also invalidates DOMA, the federal law.
sentences.zh: 奥贝格费尔案也废除了联邦法律DOMA。

sentences.en: That law also is no longer a good law because why?
sentences.zh: 那部法律也不再有效了，为什么？

sentences.en: It interferes with a constitutionally protected right to marry.
sentences.zh: 因为它干涉了宪法保护的结婚权。

sentences.en: But instead of just saying this is like, well, it's interesting background material, who cares?
sentences.zh: 但与其说这只是有趣的背景资料，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Well, in 2022, the Supreme Court decided to unrecognize the constitutionally protected right to an abortion in Dobbs v.
sentences.zh: 嗯，2022年，最高法院在“多布斯诉杰克逊妇女健康组织案”中，决定不再承认宪法保护的堕胎权。

sentences.en: Jackson Women's Health Organization.
sentences.zh: 该裁决推翻了1973年“罗诉韦德案”中首次承认的权利。

sentences.en: And that case overturned the right that was first recognized in Roe in 1973.
sentences.zh: 虽然堕胎看起来与婚姻截然不同，当然它们确实是不同的话题，但对于托马斯大法官来说，这并非无关。

sentences.en: And even though abortion might seem to be pretty distinct from marriage, and of course it is a different topic, it was not a different topic for Justice Thomas.
sentences.zh: 托马斯大法官加入了多布斯案的多数意见，但他还写了一份单独的意见书，因为他有更多话要说。

sentences.en: Justice Thomas joined the majority opinion in the Dobbs case, but he also wrote a separate opinion because he had more to say.
sentences.zh: 他想说的本质上是：看，如果我们推翻了堕胎权（我认为这是个好主意，这是他的想法），

sentences.en: And essentially his more to say was, look, if we're overturning the right to an abortion, which I think is a good idea, that's his thinking,
sentences.zh: 我们或许也应该根据法院今天所用的相同解释，重新考虑一些其他权利。

sentences.en: we might also reconsider some rights based on the same interpretation that the court issues today.
sentences.zh: 他特别点名了“奥贝格费尔诉霍奇斯案”。

sentences.en: And he calls out specifically Obergefell v.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许我们应该考虑推翻那个案子。

sentences.en: Hodges.
sentences.zh: 所以他的意见敲响了警钟，你可以想象得到。

sentences.en: Like, maybe we should think about overturning that case.
sentences.zh: 这里的想法是，看，如果托马斯大法官能说服其他四位大法官他是对的，那么这种权利可能就会受到质疑。

sentences.en: So his opinion set off alarms, as you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 你说敲响了警钟，但后来真的发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: And so the idea here is, look, if Justice Thomas can just convince four other justices that he's right, then presumably that right might be in question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，2022年，当时是拜登政府执政。

sentences.en: So you said alarm bells went off, but like, did anything actually come of that?
sentences.zh: 拜登总统签署了《尊重婚姻法案》，简称RIFMA。

sentences.en: Well, in 2022, this was the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么RIFMA做了什么？

sentences.en: President Biden signed the Respect for Marriage Act, or RIFMA.
sentences.zh: RIFMA正式废除了1996年的《捍卫婚姻法案》，对吧？

sentences.en: OK, so what does RIFMA do?
sentences.zh: 但它走得更远。

sentences.en: So RIFMA formally repeals the Defense of Marriage Act from 1996, right?
sentences.zh: RIFMA的一项条款（这是联邦法律）要求所有州对婚姻（包括同性婚姻）给予法律所称的“充分信任与尊重”，

sentences.en: But it also goes further.
sentences.zh: 它明确指出了这一点，只要这些婚姻是在某个州合法缔结的。

sentences.en: One section of RIFMA, this is the federal law, requires all states to give what the law calls full faith and credit to marriages, including same-sex marriages,
sentences.zh: 所以RIFMA并不要求一个州必须颁发同性婚姻许可。

sentences.en: which it identifies specifically, if they are lawfully performed within a state.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它不要求那些之前没做过的州现在必须去做。

sentences.en: So RIFMA doesn't require a state to license same-sex marriages.
sentences.zh: 但只要美国有一个州颁发同性婚姻许可，RIFMA这部联邦法律的效力就意味着，

sentences.en: In other words, it doesn't require a state that isn't, you know, hadn't done that before to do it.
sentences.zh: 这些婚姻在其他49个州也应受到尊重。

sentences.en: But as long as there is one state in the United States that does license same-sex marriages, the effect of RIFMA, this federal law,
sentences.zh: 记住，婚姻作为一个法律概念非常重要。

sentences.en: means that those marriages should be respected in the other 49.
sentences.zh: 当然，它在象征意义上很重要，但它还带有各种继承权、在配偶生病时探视的权利，以及各种各样的影响，

sentences.en: And remember, marriage as a legal idea is really important.
sentences.zh: 对子女的权利等等。

sentences.en: Of course, it's important symbolically, but it carries all kinds of effects of inheritance, the ability to visit your spouse while they're ill, all kinds of things,
sentences.zh: 这极其重要，对吧？

sentences.en: the rights over children, things like that.
sentences.zh: 请记住，RIFMA本质上是为了应对法院中某位大法官带来的威胁，对吧，就是因为那个原因。

sentences.en: It's extremely important, right?
sentences.zh: 那么国会能通过这项法律的原因，是否仍然与“国会可以通过一般法律”的效力条款等相关？

sentences.en: And keep in mind that RIFMA is essentially responding to this threat from one justice on the court, right, because of that.
sentences.zh: 那是其中的一部分吗？

sentences.en: So is the reason why Congress can pass this law, is it still related to the Congress may, by general laws, the effect clause, all that sort of stuff?
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Is that part of it?
sentences.zh: 原因和DOMA一样。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 国会依赖的是效力条款，即第四条中赋予国会的那部分权力。

sentences.en: It's the same reason as DOMA.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，RIFMA的意义并不大，因为奥贝格费尔案是现行法律，对吧？

sentences.en: Congress is relying on the effects clause, the power given to it, under that portion of Article 4.
sentences.zh: 但如果出于某种原因（我们希望不会发生），最高法院推翻了2015年的那个裁决，

sentences.en: So right now, RIFMA doesn't mean too much because Obergefell is the law of the land, right?
sentences.zh: 我预计我们会看到关于RIFMA含义的法律斗争，以及国会最初是否有权通过它。

sentences.en: But if for some reason, let's hope not, the Supreme Court were to overturn that decision from 2015,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对宪法第四条的解析。

sentences.en: I would expect that we'd see legal fights about the meaning of RIFMA and whether Congress actually has the authority to have passed it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: So that's kind of a sneaky way that we might see the full faith and credit clause come up in some future instance.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种我们在未来可能会看到“完全信任与尊重条款”发挥作用的隐蔽方式。

sentences.en: And that is why full faith and credit is pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么“完全信任与尊重”相当有趣的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's also, it's notable that they use that term in the law, full faith and credit, right, to harken back to this.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，他们在法律中使用了“完全信任与尊重”这个术语，对吧，这是为了呼应这一点。

sentences.en: Like, it's saying, like, if you're wondering what the constitutional basis for this is, just, like, follow the words.
sentences.zh: 就像是说，如果你想知道这背后的宪法依据是什么，只要跟着字面意思走就行了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And part of that is because, you know, it's pretty clear as a concept that if you have something, and again,
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，你知道，作为一个概念，如果拥有某样东西，而且再次强调，

sentences.en: assuming that marriage is something that is one of the things called out by the full faith and credit clause, that is protected by that clause, Congress should be able to say,
sentences.zh: 假设婚姻是“完全信任与尊重条款”所涵盖的事项之一，即受该条款保护，那么国会应该能够说，

sentences.en: hey, states, you recognize it in one state, then every state has to recognize the same thing.
sentences.zh: 嘿，各州，如果你们在一个州承认了它，那么每个州都必须承认同样的事情。

sentences.en: You'll notice what RIFMA is not doing.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到《尊重婚姻法》（RIFMA）没有做什么。

sentences.en: It is not saying there is a federally protected right to same-sex marriage because it's not super clear that Congress has the ability to do that.
sentences.zh: 它并没有说存在联邦保护的同性婚姻权利，因为国会是否有能力这样做并不十分明确。

sentences.en: And presumably, you know, Congress and President Biden were just didn't really want to go there.
sentences.zh: 而且据推测，你知道，国会和拜登总统只是真的不想触及那个层面。

sentences.en: So they kind of took a compromise measure here with full faith and credit.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在这里采取了一种折中的方案，即“完全信任与尊重”。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Makes sense.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 很有趣。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So next, Section 2 of Article 4.
sentences.zh: 接下来是第四条的第二款。

sentences.en: Section 2 is a collection of different state issues.
sentences.zh: 第二款汇集了不同的州级议题。

sentences.en: So the first clause tells us that the citizens of each state shall be entitled to all privileges and immunities of citizens in the several states.
sentences.zh: 第一项条款告诉我们，各州的公民应享有各州公民的所有特权和豁免权。

sentences.en: So, Roman, think of this as an anti-discrimination principle.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，把这看作是一项反歧视原则。

sentences.en: The clause prevents states from discriminating against citizens from other states in favor of their own.
sentences.zh: 该条款防止各州为了自身利益而歧视来自其他州的公民。

sentences.en: So that's true for many, but not all situations.
sentences.zh: 这适用于许多情况，但并非所有情况。

sentences.en: Some of the most important legal cases here have focused on things like state residency requirements,
sentences.zh: 这里一些最重要的法律案例都集中在诸如州居住要求之类的问题上，

sentences.en: that you have to live in a state for a certain time to receive some kind of benefit.
sentences.zh: 即你必须在一个州居住一定时间才能获得某种福利。

sentences.en: And states usually can't interfere with what are considered fundamental rights that are recognized under the Privileges and Immunities Clause.
sentences.zh: 而且各州通常不能干涉那些在“特权与豁免条款”下被视为基本权利的事项。

sentences.en: A good example is that the Supreme Court has said, you know, your right to pursue an occupation is something that's protected by this clause.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是最高法院曾表示，你知道，你追求职业的权利是受该条款保护的。

sentences.en: But states do have some latitude.
sentences.zh: 但各州确实拥有一定的自由裁量权。

sentences.en: They can discriminate against out-of-staters for important reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于重要原因，他们可以歧视外州人。

sentences.en: That's why you can't go to another state and just say, hey, I have the right to vote in your election.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你不能去另一个州然后说，嘿，我有权在你们的选举中投票。

sentences.en: You can't because the state has a good reason to keep voters only to the people who are within the state.
sentences.zh: 你不能这样做，因为州有充分的理由将选民限制在州内居民范围内。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So this part of Article 4 isn't too much in dispute.
sentences.zh: 所以第四条的这一部分并没有太多争议。

sentences.en: It's not very controversial.
sentences.zh: 它不是很有争议。

sentences.en: Next, the second clause here, which says,
sentences.zh: 接下来是这里的第二项条款，它写道，

sentences.en: This is known as the extradition clause.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“引渡条款”。

sentences.en: And it applies when a person is accused of a crime in one state and then flees to another.
sentences.zh: 它适用于一个人在一个州被指控犯罪后逃往另一个州的情况。

sentences.en: So the extradition clause recognizes that the governor of one state can demand from the other state that the person be forcibly sent back.
sentences.zh: 因此，引渡条款承认一个州的州长可以要求另一个州将该人强制遣返。

sentences.en: Again, it's not too controversial.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也不是很有争议。

sentences.en: But, again, this shows us another aspect in which Article 4 is about requiring, encouraging,
sentences.zh: 但再次强调，这向我们展示了第四条的另一个方面，即要求、鼓励，

sentences.en: making sure that the states play nice with one another because that's how the system should be run.
sentences.zh: 确保各州之间和睦相处，因为这才是系统应该运行的方式。

sentences.en: Instead of the states fighting against each other, discriminating against each other's citizens, or just not cooperating in some important things like criminal justice.
sentences.zh: 而不是各州之间相互争斗、歧视彼此的公民，或者在刑事司法等重要事务上不予配合。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: So third clause, and that is the fugitive slave clause.
sentences.zh: 第三项条款，即“逃亡奴隶条款”。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, we don't really need to talk about this clause, which allowed a slave owner to cross state lines, seize the fugitive enslaved person,
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，我们真的不需要讨论这个条款，它允许奴隶主跨越州界，抓捕逃亡的被奴役者，

sentences.en: go to court to prove ownership, and then receive legal authorization to go back to their home state with the enslaved person.
sentences.zh: 去法院证明所有权，然后获得法律授权，带着被奴役者回到他们所在的州。

sentences.en: You know, the entire aspect of this clause is irrelevant because of the 13th Amendment, which abolishes slavery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个条款的整个方面都已经无关紧要了，因为第十三修正案废除了奴隶制。

sentences.en: But I thought we'd pause here for a moment just to note that this is just another instance in which our foundational current document that organizes our government has a reference to slavery.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该在这里停顿一下，指出这只是我们组织政府的现行基础性文件中提及奴隶制的又一个例子。

sentences.en: It's just one more.
sentences.zh: 这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: And yet it doesn't even do so directly, right?
sentences.zh: 然而它甚至没有直接提及，对吧？

sentences.en: The fugitive slave clause doesn't even use the word slave.
sentences.zh: 逃亡奴隶条款甚至没有使用“奴隶”这个词。

sentences.en: It refers to a person held to serve or labor in one state escaping into another.
sentences.zh: 它指的是“在一个州被拘役以提供服务或劳动的个人逃往另一个州”。

sentences.en: Although, at the time, everyone understood that this reference was to enslaved people and enslaved people only.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时每个人都明白，这个指代对象就是被奴役者，且仅指被奴役者。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, here you have this kind of historical marker in the Constitution that has no legal effect anymore,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这里有宪法中这种历史性的标记，它已经没有任何法律效力了，

sentences.en: but it reminds us of kind of the very flawed origins of the document itself.
sentences.zh: 但它提醒我们，这份文件本身的起源是非常有缺陷的。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And presumably it was put here explicitly because certain slave-owning states just required it for it to be part of the Constitution for them to sign on to it.
sentences.zh: 据推测，它被明确写在这里，是因为某些蓄奴州要求将其作为宪法的一部分，他们才会签署。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And again, I mean, that's another interesting thing, too.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我的意思是，这也是另一件有趣的事情。

sentences.en: It just reflects the fact that the document itself is not an idealized one.
sentences.zh: 它反映了一个事实，即文件本身并不是理想化的。

sentences.en: It's the result of political compromise.
sentences.zh: 它是政治妥协的结果。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is sort of the baked-in part of the document.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是该文件某种程度上根深蒂固的一部分。

sentences.en: We can't escape the fact that it has this very, you know, again, flawed origin here.
sentences.zh: 我们无法逃避这样一个事实，即它有着非常，你知道，再次强调，有缺陷的起源。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: But hopefully, you know, but in some ways we escaped it by having the 13th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但希望，你知道，但在某些方面我们通过拥有第十三修正案摆脱了它。

sentences.en: So that's what amendments are for.
sentences.zh: 这就是修正案的意义所在。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Let's move right along to Section 3.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续讨论第三条。

sentences.en: And Section 3 of Article 4 has two parts.
sentences.zh: 第四条的第三条有两个部分。

sentences.en: The first part includes the Admissions Clause, and that is how we allow or admit new states to the union.
sentences.zh: 第一部分包括“准入条款”，这就是我们允许或接纳新州加入联邦的方式。

sentences.en: So, Roman, you want to read that clause?
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，你想读一下那个条款吗？

sentences.en: It's sort of interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有趣的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, you know, it seems to be a part of a new state, like when Kentucky became a state by taking a part of Virginia in 1792, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它似乎是一个新州的一部分，比如1792年肯塔基州通过从弗吉尼亚州划出一部分而成为一个州，对吧？

sentences.en: So, that part, you know, it seems to make sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，那部分，你知道，似乎说得通。

sentences.en: You don't want to chop off a part of the state without the state agreeing to do it.
sentences.zh: 你不想在未经该州同意的情况下切掉它的一部分。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And while it's not mentioned in Section 3 itself, the Supreme Court has interpreted the Admissions Clause to have what it calls an equal footing doctrine.
sentences.zh: 虽然第三条本身没有提到，但最高法院将“准入条款”解释为具有所谓的“平等地位原则”。

sentences.en: And so, the idea is a pretty simple one, that a new state, if it's going to be part of the United States and is admitted to the United States by Congress,
sentences.zh: 所以，这个想法很简单，即一个新州，如果它要成为美国的一部分，并被国会接纳进入美国，

sentences.en: it has to be admitted on equal terms as the existing ones.
sentences.zh: 它必须在与现有州平等的条件下被接纳。

sentences.en: You don't have like a secondary status state.
sentences.zh: 你不会有一个次等地位的州。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You're not like going through a probationary period.
sentences.zh: 你不是在经历试用期。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, you know, the court has said it's not in there, but we assume that that's meant in the structure of the Admissions Clause.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，法院说它没有写在里面，但我们假设在“准入条款”的结构中就是这个意思。

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: And the second part of Section 3 has what's called the Property Clause.
sentences.zh: 第三条的第二部分有所谓的“财产条款”。

sentences.en: Congress has the power to dispose of and make all needful rules and regulations respecting the territory or other property belonging to the United States.
sentences.zh: 国会有权处置并制定所有关于属于美国的领土或其他财产的必要规则和条例。

sentences.en: Now, this part gives Congress broad authority to take all kinds of actions over the land the federal government possesses.
sentences.zh: 现在，这一部分赋予了国会广泛的权力，可以对联邦政府拥有的土地采取各种行动。

sentences.en: And the clause also mentions territories, which is interesting, too, because many of our states have become states after having been a territory first, like Alaska or Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 该条款还提到了领土，这也很有趣，因为我们的许多州在成为州之前都是领土，比如阿拉斯加或夏威夷。

sentences.en: And even though the Admissions Clause doesn't require it, Congress has sometimes required a proposed state to meet some conditions before it's allowed to become a state.
sentences.zh: 即使“准入条款”没有要求，国会有时也会要求拟议的州在获准成为州之前满足某些条件。

sentences.en: Do you know about the condition that Utah had to agree to for becoming a state?
sentences.zh: 你知道犹他州在成为一个州之前必须同意的条件吗？

sentences.en: No bigamy?
sentences.zh: 禁止重婚？

sentences.en: Well, no polygamy, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，禁止多配偶制，对吧。

sentences.en: No polygamy, right, right.
sentences.zh: 禁止多配偶制，对，对。

sentences.en: So the Enabling Act by Congress that allowed Utah to become a state actually required the state to ban polygamy.
sentences.zh: 所以国会允许犹他州成为一个州的《授权法》实际上要求该州禁止多配偶制。

sentences.en: And what's even more interesting is that Utah is not allowed by the terms of its own constitution to allow polygamy unless not just Utah, but Congress agree.
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是，根据其自身宪法的条款，犹他州不允许实行多配偶制，除非不仅是犹他州，而且国会也同意。

sentences.en: In other words, Congress was so worried that the state might just go crazy with polygamy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，国会非常担心该州可能会在多配偶制问题上变得疯狂。

sentences.en: They were like, you can't even change your state constitution unless we let you on this subject.
sentences.zh: 他们当时的意思是，除非我们允许，否则你甚至不能修改你的州宪法来处理这个问题。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Congress can definitely do that.
sentences.zh: 所以国会绝对可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: If there's something that they don't like about a proposed state, they can say, you're not allowed to be a member of the club unless you do this particular thing.
sentences.zh: 如果他们对一个拟议的州有什么不满，他们可以说，除非你做这件特定的事情，否则你不允许成为俱乐部的成员。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So hypothetically, if we were to do something like, you know, Annex Greenland, not endorsing the idea.
sentences.zh: 所以假设一下，如果我们要做一些事情，比如，你知道，吞并格陵兰岛，我并不是在支持这个想法。

sentences.en: But if we were to do that, presumably the path would be Congress would give it the status of an American territory first, right,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们真的那样做了，推测路径会是国会首先给予它美国领土的地位，对吧，

sentences.en: which gives it free reign to regulate the territory under the property clause.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了它根据财产条款管理该领土的自由。

sentences.en: And then maybe it would become a state eventually.
sentences.zh: 然后也许它最终会成为一个州。

sentences.en: And if it did so,
sentences.zh: 如果它真的这样做了，

sentences.en: it could certainly require Greenland to enter into some kind of agreement that they would not do something or do something affirmatively in order to become a state.
sentences.zh: 它当然可以要求格陵兰岛达成某种协议，即为了成为一个州，他们不会做某事或会积极地做某事。

sentences.en: Although we certainly have territories, you know, like Puerto Rico, of course, that have remained a territory for a very long time,
sentences.zh: 虽然我们当然有领土，你知道，比如波多黎各，当然，已经长期保持领土状态，

sentences.en: even though there are certainly lots of folks who would like to see Puerto Rico become the 51st state.
sentences.zh: 尽管肯定有很多人希望看到波多黎各成为第51个州。

sentences.en: So this is the part of the constitution that kind of sets the ground rules for when a territory or an acquired piece of land can join the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以这是宪法中为领土或获得的土地何时可以加入美国设定基本规则的部分。

sentences.en: But it doesn't set that many ground rules.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有设定太多的基本规则。

sentences.en: It just says that they can make the ground rules, but the rules could change depending on what state you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 它只是说他们可以制定基本规则，但规则可能会根据你所讨论的州而改变。

sentences.en: Yeah, essentially, it's kind of left up to Congress, like they make the political decisions about, you know, what to do.
